testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: A ____ lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets a driver slowly apply spring brakes. A lever on the dashboard controls the valve.

questions.question: You are most likely to feel strong winds when:
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to keep your vehicle in its lane. This is a big problem when you drive out of a tunnel.

questions.question: Lights that show anti-lock brakes are not working are:
questions.explanation: Vehicles with anti-lock brakes have yellow warning lights. These lights show there is a problem with the brake system.

questions.question: Tires with tread separation are:

options.text: Acceptable if placed on the rear of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Do not use tires with tread separation. Check your tires during inspections to make sure they do not have tread separation.

questions.question: If brakes fail on a long downhill slope, the driver should:

options.text: Turn the vehicle off and then back on to reset the brakes.
Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for an escape ramp or another way to stop.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail on a downhill slope, use an escape ramp if one is available. If not, look for another way to stop, like a side road or open field.

questions.question: Skids happen when:

options.text: Tires lose their grip on the road.
There is too much weight in the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose their grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Skids happen when tires lose grip on the road. This can be caused by over-braking, over-accelerating, over-steering, or driving too fast.

questions.question: When backing with a trailer:

options.text: You should not back up in a straight line.
You should not correct drift until you are far off course.
You should pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should pull forward often to reposition the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When backing, pull forward to reposition your vehicle whenever needed. Fix drift right away by turning the steering wheel in the direction the vehicle is drifting.

questions.question: The faster you drive:

options.text: The shorter your stopping distance will be.
The longer your stopping distance will be.
The easier it will be to stop your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer your stopping distance will be.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop. Adjust your braking accordingly.

questions.question: Air tank drains should:

options.text: Only be used when it is wet outside.
Be used to drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be used to drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Air tank drains remove water and oil from the air tanks. Always drain the tanks completely when you use them.

questions.question: You may be an aggressive driver if you:

options.text: Slow down and keep a safe following distance.
Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures that could anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by being realistic about travel time, allowing for delays, keeping a safe following distance, and not making hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you block other drivers, what should you do?

options.text: Wave your arm out the window.

questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers. This warns drivers behind you (where local laws allow).

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of injury and death in work zones. Slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: When are containerized loads used?

options.text: When cargo is too large to fit on a truck.
When cargo has been or will be transported by train.

questions.correctAnswerText: When cargo has been or will be transported by train.
questions.explanation: Containerized loads are used when freight travels by rail or ship. Drivers must check that containers do not exceed safe weight limits.

questions.question: What can affect stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on speed, vehicle weight, and road surface traction.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of when to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to upshift: engine speed (RPM) and road speed (mph). Check your manual for rpm range and watch your speedometer. Time is not a factor.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand while the other rests.
With both hands for a firm grip.
Release it if the vehicle hits a bump.

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands for a firm grip.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides.

questions.question: How is alcohol removed from your body?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to wait and let your body process the alcohol.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver on the road, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, give them plenty of room and keep a safe distance.

questions.question: Why is texting while driving especially dangerous?

options.text: It distracts your mind and takes your hands off the wheel.
A message may upset the driver.
People like to read and may focus too much on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It distracts your mind and takes your hands off the wheel.
questions.explanation: Texting is dangerous because it is both a mental and physical distraction. It takes your attention from the road and requires you to remove at least one hand from the wheel.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while shifting gears, what may happen?

options.text: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble shifting into the next gear.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long, you may have difficulty shifting into the next gear. Do not force it. Return to neutral, release the clutch, match the engine speed to road speed, and try again.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread in each groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. All tires must be the same size.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: When making a left turn, you should start the turn:

options.text: Before reaching the center of the intersection
When you reach the center of the intersection or after
After your rear wheels pass the center of the intersection

questions.correctAnswerText: When you reach the center of the intersection or after
questions.explanation: Wait until you reach the center of the intersection before turning left. If you turn too early, the left side of your vehicle may hit another vehicle.

questions.question: When changing lanes, your turn signal:

options.text: Should only be used if traffic is present
Should only be used from dusk to dawn

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes.

questions.question: Leaving space between your vehicle and the car ahead is:

options.text: Not recommended, as it slows traffic flow
Recommended, as it gives you time to react to hazards
Only recommended if you have a passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Recommended, as it gives you time to react to hazards
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires space around all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to act safely if a problem occurs.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when accelerating on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels spin on a slippery surface, take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: To complete an offset back/left parking maneuver, a driver should:

options.text: Drive forward straight, then back up to the left
Back up straight, then drive forward to the left
Drive forward straight, then back up straight

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive forward straight, then back up to the left
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, drive forward straight first, then back up to the left. Park your vehicle completely within the parking space.

questions.question: When driving a 50-foot truck at 50 mph, your minimum following distance should be:
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second.

questions.question: A driver should ensure that:

options.text: Cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer

questions.explanation: Proper cargo loading is essential for safe vehicle operation. Improper loading affects handling and can damage the vehicle. It can also cause cargo to fall and cause injury or death.

questions.question: When approaching your vehicle for a pre-trip inspection, what sign indicates trouble?

options.text: A puddle of oil under the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
questions.explanation: Look under your vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel. Any fresh puddle of these fluids indicates a possible safety problem.

questions.question: Why do vehicles use multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions?

options.text: To make the vehicle run more smoothly

questions.explanation: Multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions give vehicles extra gears.

questions.question: When should cargo be checked?

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
Only by the people who load it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and every three hours or 150 miles after that. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safe and secure the whole trip.

questions.question: What should you see in properly adjusted mirrors?

options.text: A small part of the vehicle
More than half of the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: A small part of the vehicle
questions.explanation: A properly adjusted mirror shows some of the vehicle. This helps you judge how far other objects are from your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you stop a skid caused by acceleration?

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: Skids from acceleration happen on slippery roads. You can stop them by taking your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: What should you check on a power steering system?

options.text: Make sure hoses connect to the battery.

questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What happens to bridges in cold weather?

options.text: They have heaters to prevent freezing.
They freeze before other road surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before other road surfaces.
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other parts of the road. Be careful on bridges when temperatures are near freezing.

questions.question: How do you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Your vehicle must stay within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: What is bracing used for?

options.text: To make items taller in a trailer
To stop items from moving in a trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: To stop items from moving in a trailer
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting during transport. Blocking goes in front, back, and sides of cargo. Bracing goes from the top of cargo to the floor and sides.

questions.question: What is turned on by an electric switch that the brake pedal triggers?
questions.explanation: Brake lights turn on when the brake pedal is pushed. This triggers an electric switch that activates the lights.

questions.question: When should you downshift?
questions.explanation: Always downshift before going down a hill or entering a curve.

questions.question: In an engine fire, you should NOT:

options.text: Turn off the engine as soon as possible.

questions.explanation: In an engine fire, turn off the engine right away. Do not open the hood if you can help it.

questions.question: Tire load is:

options.text: Can be exceeded in cooler conditions.
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
Must be written in the shipping papers.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a given pressure.
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum weight a tire can safely carry at a given pressure. This rating is printed on the side of each tire.

questions.question: When transporting cargo, check that it is secure every:
questions.explanation: Check cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, then every three hours or 150 miles after that.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, do not use the brakes. Instead, let off the gas and push in the clutch. This will help you regain traction.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Livestock:

options.text: Should never be carried on a trailer.
Should be placed in the front of a trailer.

questions.explanation: Live animals can lean during curves and move while traveling. This makes the weight distribution unstable. Driving with livestock requires special care.

questions.question: In very hot weather, if tire air pressure is too high, you should:

options.text: Let air out of the tire.
Let the tires cool before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the tires cool before driving.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure can get dangerously high in very hot weather. Stop and let your tires cool. Do not let air out, as the pressure will drop too much when they cool.

questions.question: When turning, when should you cancel the turn signal?
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on during the whole turn. Cancel it only after the turn is done.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver crashes ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's behavior.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash involving an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance from the scene. Wait for police and tell them what you saw.

questions.question: When parking, you should not use the parking brake if:

options.text: There is snow on the ground.

questions.explanation: If your brakes are hot after coming down a steep hill, do not use the parking brake. Let the brakes cool first or you may damage them.
